title: Standing Automatic Transfers into Savings and Money Market Accounts
content:
An automatic transfer moves a fixed amount each month from a Piedmont Crescent Bank checking account into an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts. Setting one up or changing one is the owner's own instruction to move their own funds.

### Conditions on the instruction

The funding checking account must belong to the same customer as the savings account and must be in active status when the instruction is recorded; both are read from the bank's record of that checking account. The amount must be at least the smallest recurring automatic transfer amount set for the savings tier.

The transfer day is a day of the month from 1 to 28. Where that day is not a business day, the transfer runs on the next business day.

### What happens on the transfer day

On the transfer day the transfer posts to the savings account as a deposit made through the automatic transfer channel, and by that posting the funding checking account is debited. Where the checking ledger balance would go below zero, the transfer is skipped for that month, with no entry and no fee, and it never creates an overdraft.

### Stopping the instruction

Stopping the transfer sets the amount to 0.00 USD and clears the day and the funding account, effective for the next scheduled run.

### Points of judgement

*Why is the day of the month limited to 1 through 28?* Because those are the days that occur in every month.

*What happens in a month where the funding account cannot cover the transfer?* That month's run is skipped in full. Nothing posts to either account and no fee arises, and the instruction itself stands for the following month.
